mcqs.question: When representing the magnetic field produced by a straight current‑carrying wire with field lines, which statement is true?

options.A: Field lines originate from the wire and terminate at infinity.
options.B: Field lines form closed loops around the wire.
options.C: Field lines are straight lines parallel to the wire.
options.D: Field lines are present only on one side of the wire.

mcqs.answer: Field lines form closed loops around the wire.
mcqs.explanation: Magnetic field lines are continuous loops; they never start or end on any point. Around a straight conductor the lines circle the wire forming closed loops. Option A is a common misconception that magnetic lines start at the source. Option C describes electric field lines for a uniform field, not magnetic ones. Option D is incorrect because the field exists on all sides of the wire.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand field around a straight conductor
mcqs.question: A straight horizontal wire carries current from left to right. At a point P located 5 cm above the wire, what is the direction of the magnetic field?
mcqs.explanation: Using the right‑hand thumb rule, point the thumb in the direction of current (left to right). The curled fingers show the magnetic field direction; above the wire the field points out of the page. Hence option B is correct. Option A is the opposite direction, while C and D describe directions along the wire, not perpendicular to it.

mcqs.question: Two identical straight conductors are placed parallel to each other. In conductor A, current flows upward; in conductor B, current flows downward. Using the right‑hand thumb rule, which statement correctly describes the magnetic field at a point midway between the two conductors?

options.A: The fields due to both conductors are in the same direction, reinforcing each other.
options.B: The fields due to the conductors are opposite and cancel each other.
options.C: Field due to conductor A is into the page and due to B is out of the page, resulting in zero net field.
options.D: Both fields are perpendicular to the plane of the page.

mcqs.answer: The fields due to the conductors are opposite and cancel each other.
mcqs.explanation: Apply the right‑hand thumb rule to each wire. For the upward current, the field at the midpoint points into the page; for the downward current, it points out of the page. These opposite directions cancel, giving zero net field. Option A is wrong because the directions are opposite, not the same. Option C describes the same situation but splits it into two statements; the net result is still cancellation, which is captured by option B. Option D is inaccurate because the fields lie in the plane of the page, not perpendicular to it.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand field around a circular loop
mcqs.question: A circular loop of radius 10 cm carries a current I. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre of the loop?
mcqs.explanation: The magnetic field at the centre of a single circular loop is given by B = μ0 I / (2R) for a solenoid, but for a loop the correct expression is B = μ0 I / (2πR). Substituting the radius R = 0.10 m gives B = μ0 I / (2π × 0.10). Option A matches the standard formula. Options B, C, and D are variations that omit the π factor or use incorrect denominators, leading to wrong magnitudes.
